I didn't check which five holdings are VLTX's largest. I took the five names as given and had one node research each. The outlooks below rest on two short source notes per company, so treat them as headline views.

| Holding | 2027 revenue | 2027 margins |
|---|---|---|
| **Voltaris Grid (VLTG)** | Management reaffirmed guidance of C$4.2B. Backlog of C$5.1B is above that. I found no growth rate. | Operating margin near 11%, flat on 2026. |
| **Tarnwell Electric (TRNW)** | Up 6%, driven by price increases. | Operating margin rises to 14% from 12%, also on pricing. |
| **Braxen Cable (BRXC)** | Up about 2%. Volumes are flat, so the growth is cost pass-through pricing. | Under pressure from copper costs up 18%. Earnings are expected to be flat. The source gives no margin percentage. |
| **Ostrand Meters (OSTM)** | A smart-meter contract with Norvane Utilities adds about 20%. | Down one point as the Norvane rollout ramps. The notes don't say if the dip is temporary. |
| **Kelby Switchgear (KLBS)** | Down 5%, as it loses medium-voltage share to Tarnwell. | Held at 8% by restructuring. The notes don't say if 8% is a 2027 forecast or the current level. |

- **Pricing risk:** Tarnwell's gains in both revenue and margin rest on pricing, so they would shrink if volumes fall in response.
- **Restructuring risk:** Kelby's margin depends on the restructuring program staying on track.

None of the sources give dollar revenue figures, except Voltaris.
